title.narrative: Initiation of the Smart Water Resources Modelling Centre

description.narrative:
This project aims at initiating the Smart Water Resources Modelling Centre as a Centre of Excellence (CoE) in close collaboration with the Central Water Commission (CWC) and the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), India. It is part of a strategic partnership between the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, and the Ministry of Environment, Government of Denmark. The Centre is envisioned to be a leading hub for introducing best practices, state-of-the-art technology, and knowledge exchange in the areas of integrated water resources management, surface and groundwater modelling, groundwater mapping and climate-resilient water governance.
As a condition for initiating the project, it is required that a detailed workplan, budget, and timeline be drafted and submitted to the Embassy as the first activity. These documents will serve as the guiding framework for the implementation of the SDG funding and must be prepared in close coordination with the relevant Indian counterparts. It is important to underline that this workplan, budget, and timeline refers only to the activities funded under this specific SDG project and does not encompass the entire scope or operations of the CoE. It is acceptable that separate workplans, budgets, and timelines are developed for the partnerships with CWC and CGWB, reflecting the specific priorities and modalities of collaboration with each institution.
The CoE will play a key role in strengthening technical capacity within CWC and CGWB through a structured training and knowledge-sharing programme. Initial technical activities will focus on high-priority thematic areas such as flood forecasting and inundation modelling, Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) studies, and extended hydrological prediction in the context of climate change. The initiative also includes the development of a sustainability plan to ensure the long-term viability of the Centre, including its funding model, institutional mandate, and capacity retention.
